journeys.controls:
Two selected-world SYS-1 journeys. One disclosed initial public-join staging each.
All later travel, acquisition, fire construction, water, work and use are game inputs.
Disposable saves; no supplies inserted, threats removed, costs or rules overridden.

stages.label: selected public approach
logs: You light the Tallow Torch.

stages.label: acquired native bone and vessel
logs: Stone. Cold stone, and the smell of old air. Thy eyes open to darkness.
Thou art beneath the ground. Something is wrong with the world above.
Thou takest up a crude blade.
Thou takest up a leather jack.
It opens.
Thou takest the Resonant Bone Fragment.
It opens.
Thou takest the copper steeping kettle.

stages.label: measured native water and gathered fuel
logs: Progress preserved.
The world reassembles itself around you.
You move into Palewater Plain.
You take bundle of wood from the dead branch.
You take bundle of wood from the dead branch.
A dryness in the throat.
The cold seeps in.
Water fills the vessel.

stages.label: ordinary preparation busy
logs: Stone. Cold stone, and the smell of old air. Thy eyes open to darkness.
Thou art beneath the ground. Something is wrong with the world above.
Where will you set the fire?
The wood is set. A spark is still needed.
The fire takes.
The fire takes the edge off.
Where will you set it to work?
The bone steeps. The vessel must stay with the work.

stages.label: dose consumed and lexicon read
logs: The tincture is ready. Something stirs in the liquid.
Thou takest the copper steeping kettle.
Thou takest the resonant bone tincture.
A word rises from the marrow. It was always there.
[ghuurkh]: the elder.
Press [L] to open the Lexicon.
Stone. Cold stone, and the smell of old air. Thy eyes open to darkness.
Thou art beneath the ground. Something is wrong with the world above.

stages.label: returned to depleted native owners
logs: The world reassembles itself around you.
The cold seeps in.
The cold returns.
The chill passes.
Something gnaws at the edge of attention.
Thou enterest Graveiss.
Something accumulates in the silence here.
The thirst is becoming difficult to ignore.

(7, 11).name: Wight Essence Residue
(7, 11).description: A crystalline deposit found in the chest cavity. The thing that inhabited the body left this behind when it departed. What inhabited it is unclear. What it wanted is less clear still.

(7, 11).name: murk violet stem
(7, 11).eat_message: Faintly sweet and then sour. Something in it pulls at the back of the jaw.
(7, 11).description: A dark stem from the murk violet. The petals have been stripped. The remaining stalk is fibrous, faintly damp, and smells of marsh water.

(7, 11).name: Resonant Bone Fragment
(7, 11).description: A splinter of something old. The tone in it is audible if you press it against your skull and hold still. Do not hold it near bells.

(7, 11).name: prophet's eye cap
(7, 11).eat_message: Tasteless. Something shifts at the edge of sight for a moment, then is gone.
(7, 11).description: A pale, watery mushroom cap. The alchemists prized it. The cap alone is worthless — the liquid inside is what they wanted.

(7, 11).name: Herbal Dressing
(7, 11).description: A prepared herbal dressing bound in clean linen. Restores up to 12 HP when injured; consumed after one use.

(15, 13).name: copper steeping kettle
(15, 13).description: A broad copper kettle. Heavy empty, roomy over a fire.

(15, 13).name: dried soporific herb
(15, 13).description: Dried violet stem. The sedative quality persists.

(15, 13).name: clay pot
(15, 13).description: A small pot, hand-formed from river clay and fired in open flame. Crude but serviceable. Holds liquids. Survives direct heat.

(11, 15).name: Crow Jerky
(11, 15).description: Strips of dried crow meat. It tastes exactly as you would expect. It sustains you regardless.

(11, 15).name: dried provisions
(11, 15).eat_message: Dry and tasteless. It does what it needs to.
(11, 15).description: A cloth parcel of preserved travel rations. Salt-stiff, dense, neutral. Someone prepared this for a journey they did not finish.

(30, 12).name: Crow Jerky
(30, 12).description: Strips of dried crow meat. It tastes exactly as you would expect. It sustains you regardless.

(30, 12).name: dried provisions
(30, 12).eat_message: Dry and tasteless. It does what it needs to.
(30, 12).description: A cloth parcel of preserved travel rations. Salt-stiff, dense, neutral. Someone prepared this for a journey they did not finish.

(62, 26).name: clay lump
(62, 26).description: A handful of river clay, dense and slightly damp. Takes any shape pressed into it. Dries hard near heat.

(62, 26).name: bundle of wood
(62, 26).description: A loose bundle of dry branches. Snapped from dead fall.

(62, 26).name: flint shard
(62, 26).description: A sharp-edged chip knocked from a larger piece of flint.

(62, 26).name: dried provisions
(62, 26).eat_message: Dry and tasteless. It does what it needs to.
(62, 26).description: A cloth parcel of preserved travel rations. Salt-stiff, dense, neutral. Someone prepared this for a journey they did not finish.

(62, 26).name: Bone
(62, 26).description: Clean or close to it. The resonance content varies by source. A craftsman would weigh it before deciding what to do with it.

(55, 11).name: pilgrim's woe petals
(55, 11).eat_message: Dry and slightly chalky. A faint warmth follows.
(55, 11).description: Dried petals from the pilgrim's woe flower, stripped from the dark fronds. Pale as old linen. The smell is faintly medicinal.

(64, 15).name: water skin
(64, 15).drink_message: Cold and flat. The thirst retreats.
(64, 15).description: A leather skin, filled with water. The hide is old but the stitching holds. Something alive is in it still.

(64, 15).name: dried provisions
(64, 15).eat_message: Dry and tasteless. It does what it needs to.
(64, 15).description: A cloth parcel of preserved travel rations. Salt-stiff, dense, neutral. Someone prepared this for a journey they did not finish.

(64, 15).name: bitter herb
(64, 15).eat_message: Bitter. Something in it is faintly wrong. The hunger retreats slightly.
(64, 15).description: A dried sprig of something that grows near water and stone. Hedge practitioners harvest it. It is edible in the way that most things are edible — with consequences.

(64, 15).name: bundle of wood
(64, 15).description: A loose bundle of dry branches. Snapped from dead fall.

definition.concept: one whose age has made them a stratum
